title: Vector Rankline Signal Aggregator — per-route rank telemetry, cost attribution, and incident playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build a lightweight, low-cardinality signal aggregator ("rankline") for the embeddings + rerank pipeline that produces route-scoped telemetry, per-request cost attribution, and an ops playbook for P99 incidents. The aggregator will run as an intermediate stats service that consumes tracing spans and request metadata, synthesizes per-route SLOs (latency, success-rate, quality regression signals), and exports compact daily/real-time rollups to the Console. Goals: enable fast triage of regressions in ranking quality, isolate cost hotpaths by route, and reduce MTTI for rerank outages.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console shows a new 'Rankline Overview' dashboard with p50/p95 latency, token-cost-per-inference, and rerank-quality delta per route; 2) Traces for rerank requests contain a rankline id and span annotations to reconstruct the pipeline; 3) Alerts fire for route-level SLO breaches and cost anomalies and are actionable (link directly to runbook); 4) Daily aggregated chargeback table exported for billing pipeline; 5) End-to-end test that simulates a noisy query pattern and verifies aggregation correctness <95% error.
tasks: Design aggregator schema: minimal fields (route, model_variant, trace_id, step, latency_ms, token_count, score_metrics)
Add rankline id to rerank request headers and propagate through runtime (serving runtime + reranker)
Instrument spans: capture scoring_time, fetch_vectors_time, similarity_ops, cache_hit_bool
Implement lightweight consumer in observability infra to materialize route rollups (Kafka -> aggregator -> ClickHouse/BigQuery)
Backend API to expose aggregated metrics to Console and cost service
Build 'Rankline Overview' Console dashboard with per-route slices and heatmap
Create alert rules and a templated incident playbook (SLO breach, cost spike, regression detection)
Add unit/integration tests for aggregation correctness and schema evolution
Run load test with synthetic workloads to validate aggregator overhead and retention sizing
Document runbook and handoff to SRE/Oncall
decisions: Keep aggregator schema intentionally narrow to reduce cardinality; avoid user-provided arbitrary tags
Materialize both real-time (1m) and daily rollups; store raw traces for 7 days and rollups for 90 days
Use protobuf v2 for rankline events to ensure stable schema evolution
Route cost-attribution computation to billing pipeline via daily export instead of per-request billing to limit storage and downstream cost
Alert thresholds will be adaptive: fixed SLO for p95 latency, but anomaly-detection for cost spikes using historical baselines
notes: Trade-offs: Short retention of raw events keeps costs down but makes deep forensics harder; mitigations: quick sampling of full payloads on alert and ability to manually increase retention per-customer for investigations.
We considered adding user-facing tags to rollups for multi-tenant grouping; postponed to phase 2 due to cardinality risk.
Coordination required with Billing to join on route -> customer mappings for chargeback accuracy
Prototype showed aggregator adds ~0.8ms median overhead to hot path when sampling enabled at 10%; aim to keep overhead <1.5ms at 100% sampling on a single host

Phase 2 (global): 100% traffic, daily chargeback export enabled, add adaptive alerting
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose route-level retention controls to enterprise customers
